hypothesis:
Throughput is the only axis in this campaign still paying, and the control run just priced it properly. t0445 ran the champion model byte-for-byte with compile mode reverted: 2744 steps and 0.962233 against the champion's 2806 and 0.961216. So max-autotune is worth +2.26% of steps, -0.001309 of bpb -- nearly double the +0.00067 I had been assuming, and the single largest lever found in 445 trials.

That control also validated the method it is measured with. For a byte-identical model the token law predicted +0.001309 against a measured +0.001017, a residual of -0.000292, well inside the 0.00085 floor. The control variate is sound out-of-sample, which is what licenses reading a throughput change as bpb at all.

The champion's autotune uses inductor's DEFAULT gemm search space, a curated subset of block/stage/warp configurations. EXHAUSTIVE searches a much larger set for the same kernels. This model's shapes are exactly where that should matter: a 512-wide residual stream, a 2048-wide MLP and an 8192-row vocabulary are small enough that curated heuristics are unlikely to contain the best tiling, which was t0058's original argument before it timed out.

Nothing about the model changes, so the evaluation graph stays cached from the champion's own runs -- the failure that killed t0438 does not apply here.
change_summary: Two lines after torch.set_float32_matmul_precision('high'): import torch._inductor.config and set max_autotune_gemm_search_space = 'EXHAUSTIVE'. Compile mode, cache directory, model, data, optimizer and every constant are the champion's, untouched. The edit asserts the champion's autotune mode is present and that no search space is already set. Dry-run against champion source parsed.
expected_val_bpb_effect:
Step count is the mechanism here, not contention -- the registered inversion, same as t0433. If EXHAUSTIVE finds better tilings I expect +1% to +3% of steps over the champion, worth -0.0006 to -0.0017. If the curated space already contains the best configs for these shapes, steps land at the champion's 2806 and this is a clean null that closes the compile axis.
The likely failure is a TIMEOUT: EXHAUSTIVE is far slower to search, and the champion leaves only ~76s of wall-clock headroom against the 660s limit. I am registering the response now so it is not chosen afterwards -- a timeout still populates the cache with whatever configs it benchmarked, so the correct follow-up is the identical setting under a fresh source hash, exactly the t0432 -> t0433 sequence that produced the current champion. If a warm retry ALSO times out, the search is too large to amortise and the axis closes.
risk:
A timeout burns this coordinate, and I am knowingly spending a slot on a setting whose most likely single-run outcome is failure. The justification is that the failure is productive: the cache is shared and persistent, so a timed-out search leaves its benchmarked configs behind, and this is the third time that pattern would be used deliberately rather than discovered.
The durable risk is one I flagged when the champion was promoted and which grows here: cached configurations are tuned against whatever SMs and clocks were free at compile time on a shared box that has produced a 23% slow device and power capping at 697 of 700W. A larger search space means more configurations selected under one machine state and reused under others. If this wins, the confirmation runs are the place staleness would first show, as disagreement between two runs of identical source -- and I would read that as real rather than as noise.
